title: 1976-09-15_Dorothy_148.txt
concise_summary: PKD argues that his novel 'Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said' is not merely analogous to the New Testament Book of Acts but is ontologically identical to it -- a printout of the same eternal, supratemporal truth. He develops the claim that his 27-year preoccupation with irreal reality culminated in 'Tears,' where his conscious affirmation of agape as a narrative substitution logically imported Pauline theology and the hidden message was encoded for future secret Christians who, like the figure 'Thomas,' exist outside linear time in a single continuous lifetime spanning Rome c. AD 50 to the future. The entry also anatomizes the gas station scene between General Buckman and the unnamed Black man as a divinely-inspired disclosure of the police power structure's secret self-image -- a 180-degree inversion of authority PKD believes the adversarial BIP-power would experience as absolute anathema. Throughout, PKD frames his own fiction as operating through GABA-blocked metacircuits that fired sequentially, with the 2-74 anamnesis as the disinhibiting event that revealed what had been latently encoded.
key_claims: 'Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said' is not merely similar to the Book of Acts but is a printout of it -- a copy of the same eternal document, such that 'before' and 'after' have no meaning between them.
PKD's 27 years of writing about irreal reality pointed nowhere until the positing of an AD 40 Judaea latent world beneath the phenomenal world gave it retrospective coherence.

The 2-74 disinhibition event revealed that PKD had GABA-blocked brain circuits containing divine information that could only fire after the completion of 1st-stage tasks, specifically the publishing of 'Tears' in February 1974.
The girl with the golden fish necklace was not a chance encounter but a necessary next integer in a logical sequence, dictated by the completion of the prior stage of circuit-firing.

The gas station scene between General Buckman and the Black man was divinely inspired and constitutes a prophetic penetration of the police power structure's secret psychological self-image -- their identification as benevolent father figures -- and its total inversion.

Authentic secret Christians are supratemporal, not located at any one 'when'; they span from Rome c. AD 50 to the future in a single continuous lifetime, and 'Tears' was designed to be read correctly by them.
The Xerox Missive fired against PKD was an act of retaliation by the adversarial power for what 'Tears' had disclosed after 25 years of incremental preparation.

Anamnesis (2-74 / 2-75) -- the remembering-event of February 1974 and February 1975 in which blocked knowledge was recovered

Sacred time vs. linear time -- the replacement of accumulating chronological time with a more real, eternal temporal mode

autobiographical: PKD describes spending 27 years preoccupied with the irreal nature of evident reality before finding the true reality in 'Tears' -- a search retrospectively given meaning by the 2-74 revelation.

In February 1974, under the influence of a girl wearing a golden fish necklace, PKD experienced the disinhibition of GABA-blocked metacircuits, which he now theorizes was necessary and logically sequenced after the publishing of 'Tears.'
In February 1975, one year after the initial 2-74 experience, PKD glimpsed what he calls the PTG -- the Kingdom of God -- which he has not seen since but believes to be real and accessible.
PKD recalls the precise moment in 3-74 when, 'under the power of the spirit,' he perceived religious crypto-message segments -- religious code -- in 'Tears,' before Father Rasch told him about Acts.
PKD identifies the moment he recognized 'Felix' as a meaningful Latin word (not just a character name) and looked it up as the beginning of his understanding of 'Tears'' true importance.

PKD describes a dream in which someone inside the Doubleday warehouse destroyed 2,500 remaining copies of 'Tears,' which he interprets as evidence of the adversarial power's rage at the novel's disclosure.
PKD reports that the adversarial power (the lying one) sought to find and destroy the single manuscript of 'Tears' before it could be published.
PKD received the Xerox Missive as a retaliatory strike from the adversary, fired before the disinhibiting stimulus (the girl with the fish necklace) could arrive.
theological_motifs: Agape -- unconditional love as the deliberate narrative substitution in 'Tears' that logically imported Pauline theology and New Testament content
Anamnesis -- Platonic-Pauline recovery of blocked divine memory, here literalized as neural disinhibition
Sacred time (hierophanic time) -- time outside linear chronology in which eternal events are always contemporaneous
The Kingdom of God (PTG) -- the divine domain that living men can enter, glimpsed by PKD in February 1975
Supratemporal Christianity -- the Fish Christians who exist in a single continuous lifetime spanning the persecuted church of Rome c. AD 50 to the eschatological future
The Christ salvific drama -- a staged sequence of eternal events (life, death, resurrection, return as king and judge) enacted invisibly at all times
Eschatological reversal / the meek inheriting -- the total elevation of the powerless ('meek') and total doom of the 'Ins,' figured in the Buckman gas-station scene as prophecy
Divine inspiration of fiction -- the gas station scene was 'divinely inspired,' not consciously crafted; PKD is an unwitting channel of prophetic disclosure
The adversary / the lying one -- a supernatural evil power that operates through mundane agents who do not know their true supernatural role, analogous to Satan
Spurious interpolation -- the adversarial overlay that occludes true reality; requires 'complex preparation + steps' to penetrate
literary_self_ref: PKD argues that 'Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said' IS the Book of Acts -- not analogous to it but ontologically identical, a 'printout' of the same eternal document in a condition of 'ubiquitous contemporality.'
PKD reads his entire corpus from 'Imposter' through 'Tears' as a 27-year encoded disclosure of the latent AD 40 Judaean world beneath the phenomenal world, with 'Tears' as the culmination.
PKD claims VALIS (the projected novel) would add nothing to what the fiction has already disclosed -- it would only be non-fictional explication of truths the stories already told.
The Penultimate Truth is recast as a theological document -- 'a textbook study of fakes: who, what + why + how' -- within the framework of spurious interpolation.

PKD argues that the conscious affirmation of agape as a narrative device in 'Tears' imported Pauline theology through an 'inner logic' not known to him at the time of writing, suggesting unconscious or divinely guided authorship.

The gas station scene in 'Tears' (Buckman embracing the Black man) is identified as a divinely-inspired prophetic penetration of the police power structure's secret self-image, making 'Tears as a whole' absolute anathema to the BIP-authority.
PKD links the scene in 'Tears' to Acts 8 (Philip and the Ethiopian eunuch) as 'the real [counterpart], outside of time,' treating his fiction and scripture as temporally co-incident.
symbols_images: The golden fish necklace -- worn by the girl who triggered PKD's 2-74 disinhibition; the ichthus sign of the secret Christians, functioning as the external stimulus that unlocked blocked circuits
The all-night gas station -- the liminal, nocturnal setting of the Buckman scene in 'Tears'; a threshold space where the true inversion of power occurs
General Buckman hugging the Black man -- the central prophetic image; a police general (embodiment of the BIP authority) becoming a helpless child comforted by the Black man as father figure
The worm in the Rose (Blake) -- used to figure the adversary's penetration to the secret heart of the police power structure, a wound that cannot be countered
GABA-blocked circuits -- a neurological image for divine latency; the brain as a container of suppressed revelation waiting for the right stimulus to fire
The Xerox Missive -- a bureaucratic weapon; a document weaponized by the adversary as retaliation, the mundane form taken by supernatural rage
The wise old king who judges -- a dream figure brought in at the entry's close, identified with the returning Christ of Revelation enacting the final stage of the salvific drama
Felix (the word) -- the moment of etymological recognition (Latin: happy/fortunate) as the threshold of understanding; a word hiding in plain sight as a name
tensions: PKD cannot explain why the Buckman-Black man scene provokes the adversary to frenzy: 'I can't make out why' -- he can intuit the scene's meaning to himself but not fully reconstruct the adversary's psychology from inside it.

PKD oscillates between claiming 'Tears' was consciously crafted (agape as deliberate substitution) and insisting the deeper theological content was 'accidental, insofar as I was concerned' and divinely inspired -- authorial intention and divine channel are unresolved.
PKD admits he cannot be certain the novel was 'designed to be read correctly by those in the future' -- 'I can't be sure' -- leaving open whether the encoding was intentional or merely discoverable.

PKD speculates that even without the 2-74 revelations he 'probably' would not have discerned the Acts material in 'Tears' -- suggesting the interpretation is contingent on the visionary state, not textually self-evident.

The framework requires that mundane agents of the adversary 'would not know either their true supernatural role or leader' and are 'more deceived than anyone else' -- but this makes the conspiracy unfalsifiable, as any denial by agents confirms their deception.

PKD's claim that the Christ salvific drama is 'enacted invisibly (at all times)' and that 'The Kingdom has come, (whether all men can see it or not)' sits in tension with his earlier admission that since 2-75 he has 'never seen it' again.
evidence_quotes: "I now believe it was designed to be read correctly by those in the future, but I can't be sure. Anyhow, by authentic, secret Xtians, wherever they are - whenever - my God - they aren't at any one 'when' - that's the whole point. They are supratemporal: Rome c. AD 50 to our future: they, like 'Thomas,' spans it all, the one continuous lifetime!"

"So in a very real sense 'Tears' wasn't written later than 'Acts' but is 'Acts'! It's a printout of 'Acts' like a copy, one of many. We're speaking of a ubiquitous contemporality, with 'before' not + 'after' having no meaning. It is always the some thing or piece - not like it, but of itself."
"That the scene was accidental, insofar as I was concerned - they'd never guess that. In truth, it was divinely inspired. But they'd not guess that either."

"I'll never forget how it felt in 3-74 when, under the power of the spirit, I saw religious crypto-message segments - religious code - in 'Tears' - + this was before Father Rasch told me about 'Acts.' That first moment, when I recognized Felix as a word + not just a name - + looked it up."

"The black man becomes a father figure + Buckman a child in distress. Whom the black man comforts. For all I know, the bedrock role which the cop sees himself as playing is benevolent authority father figure, + the Negro as simple child. Well, this scene in 'Tears' turns it 180° around."
uncertainty_flags: The 'Bechwek' reference ('the real [Bechwek], outside of time') is bracketed and apparently a transcription uncertainty -- the intended name is unclear; it may refer to the Ethiopian eunuch of Acts 8 or another figure.
PKD references 'Blood Money' as a lesser novel -- this is almost certainly Counter-Clock World (also known under other working titles), but the nickname is non-standard and scholars should verify.
The 'Frolix 8' reference is ambiguous: PKD had two novels with related titles (Our Friends from Frolix 8 and A Maze of Death); context suggests Our Friends from Frolix 8 but is not definitive.

Multiple passages contain '[..]' transcription gaps indicating illegible or missing text in the source manuscript, particularly in the discussion of why the Buckman scene provokes the adversary and in the description of the dream figure of the wise old king.

PKD's identification of 'Thomas' as a supratemporal figure who 'spans it all, the one continuous lifetime' is unclear -- this may refer to the Gospel of Thomas, the Apostle Thomas, or PKD's own alter ego 'Thomas' from his later fiction (VALIS), and the referent shifts the theological argument significantly.

The claim that the adversary 'sought to find + kill the single MS of the novel to no avail' is stated without elaboration; it is unclear whether this refers to a literal event PKD believes occurred or a metaphysical-level attack.

raw_text: think I told the whole message, at least so far as I know it. "VALIS" would be no more that an explication + non-fictional confirmation of truths already told. + I'm not even considering the material in such lesser novels as "Sheep" + "Frolix 8," etc. + "Clans." "Game-players of Titan," "Simulacra" + "Blood Money"; there are trace amounts in them which fill in details of the picture (like "Now Wait for Last Year," eg). + "Penultimate Truth" is a textbook study of fakes: who, what + why + how. Without the positing of the AD 40 Judaea latent world beneath the obvious phenomenal world, my 27 years of preoccupation with the irreality of evident reality - it makes no sense - it points nowhere. We gain nothing. Am I saying everything is unreal? That doesn't make sense; in comparison with what? At best it would have been a sophomoric solipsism - which it was not. I was searching for the true reality within or beyond - + in "Tears" I found it. As was both proved + explicated for me in 2/74 / 75. I can even speculate (run a fantasy number) that the girl with the Golden Fish necklace either showed up or at the least happened to disinhibit my circuits because I had shown, in "Tears," that on some (latent within me) level I knew. It sure was a long search. Finally, it was accomplished by abolishing linear or accumulating time in favor of another, more real time which is called "sacred time." The final step of the journey was finding the PTG i.e. the Kingdom of God - i.e. where God rules. That didn't come until one year later: in 2/75. Since then I have never seen it but I know it is somewhere, + living men can enter it. To throw off the occluding power of the spurous interpolation evidentally requires much complex preparation + steps. The power to command cognative + perceptual assent by it is virtually [vital]. Where is the weakpoint for entry? Doubts, at first; such as I substituted affirmation must without warning be made the statement of what is. Consciously, in writing "Tears," I intended agapē is be the substituted affirmantion. This by virtue of its intrinsic nature, led to the N.T. in which the value of agapē is first presented, in history. So the nature of my deliberate affirmation brought in a linkage with the N.T. + in particular St. Paul ("Acts" describes a major part of the life of St Paul). Thus in a sense the "Acts" material was driven into existence in my novel by an inner logic, but not one known to me. But even if we create a theory that showed that unconsciously I was familiar with "Acts" we are still left with the 2-74 anamnesis; or rather, the 2-74 anamnesis should be the clue to the correct theory as to how the "Acts" material came to be in "Tears." The 2-74 disinhibition demonstrated that I had GABA-blocked circuits full of information [all during] the external disinhibiting stimulus. Which, logically, was certain to come - otherwise, why the (contents of) the circuits? As I originally spoke of them, they were "2nd stage metacircuits to fire only upon the completion of all 1st stage firing...which finished up with the publishing in 2-74 of "Tears." Logically, the next stage would be the 2nd stage metacircuit disinhibition + firing. Therefore we are [..] to view the appearing of the girl + her Fish Necklace as dictated by necessity (i.e. deliberate, not chance); [..] was logically the next integer in the sequence. Also it had to come right away. Before the evil spear, the Xerox Missive was fired in rage (in vengence). The evil interpolating power was well aware of what I had, in "Tears," disclosed after 25 years of leading up to it story by story, novel by novel, step by step. If the whole overview as to the deliverate spurious interpolations is true, then it would follow that "Tears" would incur the wrath of the lying one. Had he not sought to find + kill the single MS of the novel to no avail? (I presume that his mundane agents would not know either their true supernatural role or leader.) (They are more deceived that anyone else.) Within the deluded thought-system of evil + its ones, the figure of the Black man at the all night gas station must symbolize something other than or more than it symbolizes to me. First of all, it would be of maximum provocative offense (as witness my dream as to why someone inside Doubleday warehouse trashed the 2500 remaining copies. It would incite them to frenzy. But I can't make out why. Is the physical hugging of a black man by a [..] (white) police official the ultimate insult to the enemy + doubly so because I, the author, can't even empathize the reason or meaning? Of course, if the "enemy" spent years attacking Dr King + eventually actually assassinating him, this might be the sine quo non! What they consider the "enemy". This is 180° from their stance. Does it even imply knowledge of their stance, as if I "know more about them than they do themselves?" [..] to reverse my dictum about them - i.e. the police vis-a-vis [..]? It is the total collapse of the police stance. It isn't even defeat (as by force of arms); it is inner selling out, by them to us - as if they (symbolized by General Buckman) had been transmuted by a ghastly alchemy (to them) into us? A careful scrutiny of that scene in "Tears" points to the fact that Buckman turns to the black man to help. I guess, for them, this is the unthinkable carried to its limits. It goes even beyond equality or brotherhood. The black man becomes a father figure + Buckman a child in distress. Whom the black man comforts. For all I know, the bedrock role which the cop sees himself as playing is benevolent authority father figure, + the Negro as simple child. Well, this scene in "Tears" turns it 180° around. Horrors, if the cop has so viewed himself vs the Negro, the apotheosis of heresy! He, the police high official, is the frightened child - + the Black man as father figure comforts him + instructs him authoritatively - with advice, adult parental advice. Did I penetrate to the secret point of the police self image - + described not just its fall but it's antithesis? Thus this scene (hence, "Tears" as a whole is absolute anathema to the authorities; nothing could affront - or undermine - them more - + they alone would know it...we wouldn't. So the gas station scene in "Tears" suggests that I got my hands on a top secret psychological fact about the police + exploited (sic) it for all it was worth. "Thou art sick, oh Rose - the worm has ~ " etc. penetrates to its secret heart + killed it. As a prophetic statement, that scene could not be topped in the - to them - ominous intensity. The senior police official will ask the negro what to do, will become totally psychologically a dependent child vis-a-vis him. "Make it all right, [Darling]" I'll bet when the fuzz higherups read "Tears" they shit bricks, too bad, + to them (but unnoticed by me) the Black Man disclosed a statute violation - his 3 kids - + Buckman not only failed to bust him but failed even to notice the alternate world; officer cypher clerk at Army Central would see it, instead, as moral degeneracy. Ugh! the last time of the last bastion of decency has fallen! To write this final affront the author (me) must have penetrated to the core of "our" (the police) mind + figured out how we think at the ultimate level (which we correctly keep secret). That the scene was accidental, insofar as I was concerned - they'd never guess that. In truth, it was divinely inspired. But they'd not guess that either. I imagine this morally objectionable stuff being circulated! The fuzz mind revealed for all to see -naked, helpless, exposed to this absolute shame. We are talking about a sudden total reversal of things: the Black Boy has become a man, + the Man has become a helpless child. What more thorough a revolution can be imagined? This is not merely a political, class or ideological revolution - it goes deeper. It is nameless, from a sociological standpoint. + what can be done to counter [..] is unspeakable, really: it is the unsaid + unsayably said. It is an archetype of archetypes, it is the final confrontation + subsequent metamorphosis. Perhaps in Christian terms it can be explained - + thus, again we are brought back to the scene in "Acts" between Philip + the Black Man: the real [Bechwek], outside of time. But ah! What I know now, as of 2-74 / 75: how explicated the mystery has become! Perhaps I really know enough: the main sense of it. Suppose I'd just only discerned the "Acts" material in "Tears" - + not had the 2-74 / 75 revelations + anamnesis I'd never probably even understand. But I'd probably not ever have discerned the "Acts" material in that case. I'll never forget how it felt in 3-74 when, under the power of the spirit, I saw religious crypto-message segments - religious code - in "Tears" - + this was before Father Rasch told me about "Acts." That first moment, when I recognized Felix as a word + not just a name - + looked it up. At that moment I began to understand the importance of "Tears" - that it was a bulk for a tiny but important hidden message. I now believe it was designed to be read correctly by those in the future, but I can't be sure. Anyhow, by authentic, secret Xtians, wherever they are - whenever - my God - they aren't at any one "when" - that's the whole point. They are supratemporal: Rome c. AD 50 to our future: they, like "Thomas," spans it all, the one continuous lifetime! The original Xtians are - have been - alive up to today + into the future! That is one of the main disclosures! So in a very real sense "Tears" wasn't written later than "Acts" but is "Acts"! It's a printout of "Acts" like a copy, one of many. We're speaking of a ubiquitous contemporality, with "before" not + "after" having no meaning. It is always the some thing or piece - not like it, but of itself. So the Fuzz would not view the all night gas station scene in terms of the feelings expressed (i.e. love + compassion) but in terms of their own yardstick: relative authority - i.e. power. In which case that scene is, for them, a truly sinister one. Buckman has fallen to the very bottommost rung. It is no longer a question even of Buckman vs Taverner; it is even more fundamental. The power-structure's loss is complete + not relative. There is no lower that Buckman can fall. We are reading an account (or rather prophecy - + an accurate one) of total doom to the "Ins." + a total elevation of the "meek" or powerless. Now, if the dream figure of the wise old king who judges is brought in - we have the actual [..]. The final part of the Christ drama (which is not in "Acts" but in "Revelation") has, supra-temporally, played itself out. Christ has returned as king + judges; there is no more stages to the eternal drama the stupendous reversal of the end-times which eternally is acted out.
